operations.summary: Create a project.
Name a shared interface by the paths that define it.
Start a team draft (a spec) in a project.
Enroll the Lead, Developer or QA of a draft with a credential digest.
Launch a complete draft as a team.
Change a team's name; its id stays.
Pause a team: it cannot start or advance work until resumed.
Resume a suspended team.
Stop a team for good, keeping its history.
Record which Moo pane runs an agent, and with which provider.
Remove an agent's pane binding.
Ask for a temporary specialist, within bounds.
Start the specialist for an authorized recruitment.
The specialist hands off its deliverable with evidence.
The Lead accepts or rejects a specialist's handoff.
Cancel a specialist engagement.
Post a message to the team, a role or one agent (the audience field).
Record project or team knowledge.
Assign a task to the team's Developer.
Change which tasks a task waits for.
The Developer accepts an assigned task.
The Developer hands a task to QA with evidence.
QA accepts or sends back a handoff (a decision record).
The Lead finalizes a QA-accepted task (a decision record).
The Lead cancels a task (a decision record).
The Owner records what happened to a dispatch attempt.
The Lead retries a failed dispatch, within bounds.
Ask the Owner to authorize one exact protected action.
The Owner approves or denies. Never reachable through chat.
The Owner revokes a pending or unused approval.
Spend an approval once, for exactly the approved action.
Record a team's exclusive worktree path and branch.
Release a worktree; it is never deleted by Teams.
Say whether a released, never-used worktree is safe to delete.
Queue a branch for integration with its paths and test evidence.
QA records the review of a queued integration.
The Owner resolves a cross-team conflict.
The receiving Lead acknowledges a change notice.
Withdraw a queued integration.
The Owner starts a merge, spending an exact approval. No force option.
The Owner records the merge that landed.
The Owner records that a merge did not land.
Declare a provider, its capabilities, models and how it meters usage. Declared, never verified.
Prefer a provider and model for a role (lead, developer, qa, specialist or specialist:<specialty>).
Assign a declared provider to a team's role, if it offers what the role needs.
A Lead changes a role's provider mid-run, spending an Owner approval for exactly that change.
Turn a goal into a reviewable plan: team draft, tasks and dependencies, justified specialists and provider choices, all explained.
Change a draft plan before launch: tasks, dependencies, specialists, providers, team name.
Discard a draft plan.
Record that a plan became a team (done by teams.plans.launch.v1).

sample.summary: The OAuth change is done and reviewed.

operations.summary: Record a summary or a specialist's role context, with its sources and validity.
Replace a note with a newer one; the old one is no longer served.
The Owner accepts a proposed requirement or ADR so agents are told about it.
The Owner replaces an accepted requirement or ADR with another entry.
Raise a bounded disagreement with two pieces of conflicting evidence.
A peer gives their view (at most two peers).
The Lead settles a non-architectural dispute after a peer has responded.
The Owner decides an escalated or architectural dispute.
The Owner's harness reports usage; only a provider declared as metered may report it as metered.
Set a team's limits on reliably metered cost and tokens. Estimates never enforce.
Idle, release or resume an agent: idle takes no new work, release also revokes its credential.
